title: Ampleness lifts along a first order thickening of Noetherian schemes
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of Noetherian schemes (schemes [def-pc-scheme] that are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]) whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] has square zero, $\mathcal I^2=0$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $j^*\mathcal L$ its pullback to $Z$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. If $j^*\mathcal L$ is ample on $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then $\mathcal L$ is ample on $X$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS (coherent-lemma-ample-on-reduction, coherent.tex line 4737), proof, second and third paragraphs (the case $\mathcal I^2=0$): the exact sequence $0\to\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\to\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\to i_*i^*\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\to0$, Morphisms 01QY, the boundary derivation Cohomology 0B8S, Lemma 01XR (via 09MR) and Lemma 01YQ

proof.text: The Mathlib support of a positive power of an ideal sheaf equals its support. Taking support in j.ker^2=bot gives j.ker.support=top by support_bot. Mathlib Hom.support_ker identifies this support with the closure of the image of j. The image is closed because j is a closed immersion. Thus j is surjective.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Use invertible_pullback_tensor to register the invertibility of N=(tensorPullback j).obj L. For any x in X, choose z with j(z)=x by step 1. Unpack ampleness of N at z to obtain n>0, a section s of N^n, and an affine open U=Z_s containing z. Apply the single-section power-locus lifting theorem to obtain k>0 and t in Gamma(X,L^(n*k)), with j(zeta) in X_t iff zeta is in U for every zeta in Z.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Tensor powers of an invertible module are invertible (the proved source instance IsInvertible.tensorPow in ProjectionFormula). Apply nonvanishing_section_trivializes to L^(n*k) and t to get an open V whose underlying set is X_t. Extensionality and the lifting equivalence show j^{-1}(V)=U. In particular x=j(z) lies in V.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Restrict j to V. This restriction is a closed immersion by the Mathlib restriction instance, hence finite. Its source j^{-1}(V)=U is affine. Its underlying map is surjective: for v in V choose z with j(z)=v, and the preimage membership proof supplies a point of j^{-1}(V). Since X is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, it is Noetherian; every open of its Noetherian topological space is compact, and open subschemes are locally Noetherian. Thus V is Noetherian. Apply finite-surjective affine descent to j restricted to V to conclude V is affine.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Use the given CompactSpace X for the compactness clause of IsAmple. For every x the preceding steps produce the section t of L^(n*k) and affine open V=X_t containing x. Nat.mul_pos proves n*k>0. These witnesses are exactly the second clause of IsAmple, so L is ample.
